headline: Chip Rout Drags Market Lower at Midday as Healthcare Names Hold Up
body_html:
Stocks are under heavy pressure at midday Thursday, with 380 of the 524 names we track lower and only 140 higher. Prices are not final. Semiconductors dominate the tape, down 9.89% as a group, a far steeper fall than any other sector. Sandisk is off 18.35% and MaxLinear 17.42%.

The damage elsewhere is milder but still wide. Industrials are down 2.33%, Materials 2.14%, Consumer 1.82%, Software 1.14% and Energy 0.76%. Homebuilders, off 0.33%, and Healthcare, off 0.25%, are the firmest groups, though still in the red. Healthcare also supplies the standout mover, ADMA Biologics, up 24.48%. Vericel is up 16.79%, Progyny 13.16% and U.S. Physical Therapy 11.28%. EPAM Systems has gained 16.96% and Motorola Solutions 9.96%. On the downside, Remitly has dropped 21.18%.

The backdrop is crowded. The Bank of England has delivered its first rate hike in three years, and Asian fuel oil prices have slid on hopes of an Iran de-escalation, even as reports of tanker incidents near the Strait of Hormuz continue. Into the close, watch whether the chip selloff steadies, whether the decliners keep outnumbering gainers, and what the Gulf headlines bring ahead of Friday, November 6.

briefs.headline: Chip stocks take the brunt of the selling
briefs.body: Semiconductors are down 9.89% at midday, the weakest group by a wide margin. Sandisk has fallen 18.35% and MaxLinear 17.42%. Prices are not final, but the memory and communications-chip names are setting the tone for the whole session.

briefs.headline: Healthcare supplies most of the winners
briefs.body: ADMA Biologics leads our gainers, up 24.48%, followed by Vericel at 16.79%, Progyny at 13.16% and U.S. Physical Therapy at 11.28%. Healthcare as a group is down only 0.25%, the smallest sector loss on the board.

briefs.headline: Consumer names slip, with two sharp drops
briefs.body: Dutch Bros is down 17.31% and Steven Madden 17.15%, helping pull the Consumer group down 1.82%. Remitly, a payments name, is the biggest decliner we track, off 21.18%. Bloom Energy has also dropped 18.62%.

briefs.headline: Bank of England lifts rates for the first time in three years
briefs.body: The central bank's rate hike pushed gilt yields higher. It is the first increase in three years, and investors are likely to weigh what a tightening in Britain means for other central banks and for global bond markets.

briefs.headline: Oil slides on Iran hopes while Hormuz stays tense
briefs.body: Asian fuel oil benchmarks fell as traders priced in a possible de-escalation with Iran. Yet Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported fires on two tankers and a tugboat in the Strait of Hormuz, and a separate tanker was struck north of Qatar. Indian shares posted their biggest gains in seven months on the oil drop.

briefs.headline: Washington's new balance of power draws economic scrutiny
briefs.body: After strong Democratic election results, analysts are asking what a shifted Congress could mean for the economy. Several tax proposals aimed at wealthy Americans could return to the agenda. In Asia, some hope the change brings relief from tariffs and the Iran conflict.
